transcript: Some people are ardently against screens in theater pieces, but if you're into it, put Nothing Can Take You from The Hand of God on your list. This new play at Playwrights Horizons is about a writer who goes back to her hometown to do some possible damage control with the place and community she's written about. Carrying a load of religious trauma as a queer person who grew up in the Evangelical South, she's now revisiting those who harmed her, some of whom remember things happening very differently. These scenes are interspersed with audio bytes from a completely separate scene, one where the writer is being interviewed about her book and its subjects. This often complicates our perceptions of whatever character we're currently watching. with Jen Tullock being the sole cast member and playing every character, there are some similarities to the recent production of Dorian Gray on Broadway. This one, too, uses a myriad of different angles and cameras, creating a cinematic and documentary-esque experience. It's an intimate and impressive showcase of projection design and range from an acting standpoint. I think it’ll thematically resonate with some more than others, and it didn't quite come to a satisfying conclusion for me, but I think it makes a strong thesis statement about the blurriness of our truths that don't only belong to us. With that, another program for my collection.
